title: Planck 2018 results. VI. Cosmological parameters
authors: Planck Collaboration; N. Aghanim et al.
selectedBecause: Well-characterized CMB reference with published parameters and assumptions.
notes: 68% marginalized means, not a universal consensus or a joint maximum-likelihood vector. Curvature and w are fixed model assumptions. Massive-neutrino density in the app is a residual from rounded Ωm and Ωcb; not an exact 0.06-eV conversion.

title: DESI DR2 Lyα forest full-shape cosmological constraints
dataset: DR2 BAO + Lyα full shape + CMB + DES-Dovekie
selectedBecause: Latest reviewed 2026 collaboration update, including revised combinations.
notes: Preprint; Table 3, 68% marginalized means. Baryon/neutrino split in the preset is a declared reference approximation. Lyα shifts toward ΛCDM; reported evolving-DE preference is 2.7σ with CMB and 3.2σ with selected SNe. These are not fate probabilities. CPL future behavior is unvalidated.

title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of BAO and cosmological constraints
notes: March 2025 result: evolving-DE preference 2.8–4.2σ depends on the supernova compilation. Newer results also change data combinations; significance comparison is not a controlled one-probe substitution.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: DR6 Power Spectra, Likelihoods and ΛCDM Parameters
selectedBecause: Independent high-resolution CMB measurements and updated combinations.
notes: P-ACT includes Planck. H0=67.62±0.50 for P-ACT alone; 68.43±0.27 for P-ACT+lensing+DESI DR2 under flat ΛCDM. App density composition and Ωm sampling width for the P-ACT-H0 illustration are explicitly illustrative, not an ACT fit vector.

title: A small Magellanic Cloud distance anchor for the Hubble constant
authors: A. G. Riess et al.; SH0ES
dataset: Cepheid–supernova distance ladder with four anchors
selectedBecause: Documents a distinct local H0 inference and the Hubble tension.
notes: H0=73.17±0.86 km/s/Mpc. Do not average with CMB-derived H0 without a joint likelihood and explicit assumptions.

title: The Pantheon+ Analysis: Cosmological Constraints
notes: Uncalibrated supernovae do not determine absolute H0. Flat ΛCDM Ωm=0.334±0.018 for SNe alone.

title: Euclid data release timeline — August 2026 update
authors: NASA Euclid Science Center at IPAC
selectedBecause: Avoids inventing an unreleased Euclid cosmology posterior.
notes: Q2 June 24 2026; DR1 Foundation scheduled November 2026 and Complete mid-2027 at review time. Schedule is subject to change.

title: The Temperature of the Cosmic Microwave Background
notes: T0=2.72548±0.00057 K, rounded to 2.7255 K. Adiabatic photon cooling T∝a⁻¹; nonthermal daughter radiation is distinct.

title: Search for proton decay via p→e+π0 and p→μ+π0 in Super-Kamiokande I–IV
authors: Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; A. Takenaka et al.
notes: No established decay. Partial lifetime τ/B, not total lifetime: e+π0 >2.4×10^34 yr; μ+π0 >1.6×10^34 yr at 90% CL. A lower bound is not a forecast lifetime.

title: Search for proton decay into a single charged antilepton and a massless invisible particle
authors: Super-Kamiokande Collaboration; Y. M. Liu et al.
notes: Preprint. No significant signal; bounds apply to the specified invisible-particle channels, not universally to all proton decays.

title: A test of electric charge conservation with Borexino
authors: Borexino Collaboration; M. Agostini et al.
selectedBecause: Experimental bound on a hypothetical electron decay channel.
notes: e−→νγ lifetime >6.6×10^28 yr at 90% CL. This tests a charge-violating channel; electron decay is disabled by default.

title: Particle creation by black holes
selectedBecause: Foundational Hawking temperature and evaporation physics.
notes: App uses isolated neutral nonrotating blackbody approximation, not exact greybody/spin/species evolution. T=ℏc³/(8πGkB M).

title: Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole
selectedBecause: Documents corrections omitted from the ideal evaporation coefficient.
notes: The app's τ=5120πG²M³/(ℏc⁴) is an ideal blackbody estimate; Page's particle emission rates are not implemented. Quantum-gravity endpoint is unknown.

title: A Dying Universe: The Long-Term Fate and Evolution of Astrophysical Objects
authors: F. C. Adams and G. Laughlin
notes: Historical theoretical synthesis, not modern observational precision. Stellar fraction logistic midpoint 10^12.5 yr and slope 1.4 in the app are explicitly chosen illustrative proxy parameters, not fitted values.

title: Black dwarf supernova in the far future
selectedBecause: Shows why stable remnants need not vanish after black-hole evaporation.
notes: Conditional black-dwarf-supernova onset around 10^1100 yr, beyond this application's 10^1000 endpoint. Not included as a numerical process.

title: Phantom Energy and Cosmic Doomsday
authors: R. R. Caldwell, M. Kamionkowski and N. N. Weinberg
selectedBecause: Conditional finite-time Big Rip and analytic benchmark.
notes: Persistent w<−1 can make the future proper-time integral converge. This is not observational evidence for a Big Rip.

title: Vacuum Stability in the Standard Model and Beyond
authors: G. Hiller, T. Höhne, D. F. Litim and T. Steudtner
dataset: Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model stability analysis
selectedBecause: Documents strong theoretical and parameter dependence.
notes: No vacuum lifetime from this source is used. A user-selected local Poisson clock is only a toy model, not a four-volume nucleation calculation.

title: Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation
authors: G. W. Gibbons and S. W. Hawking
selectedBecause: de Sitter horizon temperature and entropy, with restricted domain.
notes: T_dS=ℏH/(2πkB); this is distinct from redshifted CMB T. The Hubble radius is not generally the event horizon. Horizon entropy shown only for the de Sitter limit.

title: On the curvature of space
selectedBecause: Foundational homogeneous expansion and recollapse equations.
notes: The simulator assumes an isotropic homogeneous background with specified fluid equations of state. It does not evolve perturbations.
